questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — closures.

options.misconception: Assuming the closure resets each call

questions.explanation: The closure keeps n alive between calls; the first invocation raises it to 4001 and the second to 4002. Each call mutates the same captured binding. The printed value is 4002, while the alternatives come from counting only the first increment, assuming the closure resets each call and counting three increments.
questions.hint: A closure retains the variable, it does not copy it per call.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — call binding.

options.misconception: Adding one to the bound property
Assuming the detached function loses its value

questions.explanation: call explicitly sets this to obj, so get reads v and returns 4001. Without call, the detached function would not have obj as its receiver. The printed value is 4001, while the alternatives come from assuming the detached function loses its value, guessing a default numeric result and adding one to the bound property.
questions.hint: call supplies the receiver explicitly at invocation time.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — defaults.
questions.explanation: A default parameter is used when the argument is omitted, so label returns 4002. Passing undefined explicitly would also trigger the default. Carrying the operation through gives 4002; common slips include assuming a missing argument becomes zero and thinking defaults do not apply to calls.
questions.hint: Defaults apply when an argument is missing or undefined.
